# LabFlow documentation

> Documentation for LabFlow, a multi-tenant laboratory information system for clinical laboratories, fronted by a public directory where patients find laboratories. Built and maintained by Ahsan Mahmood (https://aoneahsan.com).

LabFlow records the clinical laboratory's work: patients, a test catalogue with panels and reference
ranges, orders, specimens with an append-only chain of custody, accessioning, barcode labels, result
entry at the bench, result review, and release gated by the releasing person's role. A released result
is amended by adding a new version, never by overwriting — the original stays readable, with who
changed it and why.

The backend is hosted Postgres on Supabase. Every row belongs to a laboratory and row-level security
refuses a read or a write that crosses that boundary, so isolation is a property of the database
rather than of application code that has to remember. Firebase serves the static web build and holds
no user data: there is no Firestore, no Firebase Authentication and no Cloud Functions.

Honest framing, because this is the part most documentation gets wrong: **LabFlow is
HIPAA-conscious, not "HIPAA-compliant"** — compliance is a property of an organisation and its
processes, and no software can hold it on your behalf. There is no FDA, CAP, CLIA or SOC 2
attestation. LabFlow is laboratory software, not a medical device, and it interprets nothing.

**What is built:** the public surface, identity and laboratory setup, settings, user management, the
form builder, and the clinical spine listed above.

**What is NOT built, and is not claimed anywhere:** billing and invoicing, inventory, equipment,
quality control runs, the compliance suite, e-signatures, the SOP library, workflow automation,
appointments, home collection, field capture, the patient portal, the clinician application,
reports and analytics, and HL7 v2 / FHIR interoperability. There is no public API. There is no
browser extension and no EMR add-on. There is **no iOS application in any form**.

## Documentation

- [Introduction](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/intro): what LabFlow is, what it runs on, and what it does not do.
- [Quick start](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/getting-started/quick-start): from an account to a released result.
- [Create or join a laboratory](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/getting-started/create-or-join-a-laboratory): the two ways in, and what each needs.
- [Finding your way around](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/getting-started/finding-your-way-around): the shape of the application.
- [Architecture overview](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/architecture/overview): the stack, and where each thing lives.
- [Tenancy and row-level security](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/architecture/tenancy-and-rls): how one laboratory is kept out of another's records.
- [Records and trails](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/architecture/records-and-trails): custody, audit, result versions, and the one-writer rule.
- [User guide](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/user-guide/overview): one page per shipped area, indexed by task.
- [Roadmap](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/roadmap): what is not built, stated plainly.
- [Hosting and publishing](https://labflow-docs.aoneahsan.com/docs/deployment/overview): how the application and this site are served.
